newsitem.title: YEMEN: Four Dutch tourists held hostage in Yemen.
newsitem.headline: Four Dutch tourists held hostage in Yemen.

text.p: Four Dutch tourists kidnapped by tribesmen in Yemen were spending their third day in captivity on Saturday as military forces surrounded the area to try to secure their release, a Yemeni official said.
It is the second kidnapping involving Dutch holidaymakers this month.
"Four Dutch tourists are still being held by the tribesmen," the official told Reuters.
He said they had been abducted on Thursday in the Khawlan area, about 65 km (40 miles) east of the capital Sanaa.
The official said a strong military force had been sent to the area and had surrounded the kidnappers.
Yemeni authorities on December 19 freed five Dutch tourists who were abducted and briefly held by tribesmen while touring an area 240 km (150 miles) north of Sanaa.
In recent years, tribes in Yemen with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped tourists or other foreigners as bargaining chips.
The tribes' demands have usually involved land or water issues, and have rarely been political. There have been no reported casualties from the abductions.
